Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about Globex Retail's use cases (localized product descriptions, customer support triage in DE/FR/ES, and regional search rewrite). As promised, here's a succinct recap and proposed next steps for the eval/POC.

Recap:
- Primary goals: 1) match current EN quality in DE/FR/ES/IT/JA/KO, 2) keep p50 latency under 500ms for inference on a dedicated pool, 3) establish a regression gate for any model swap.
- Regulatory note: you flagged EU data residency and auditability requirements (we'll scope VPC/private deploy options).

Recommended eval plan (2 weeks):
1) Run automated evals and human ratings across a ~2k example prompt set per locale (attached prompt_sets_multilingual_v1.zip).
2) Models to include: redwood-13B-multilingual-quant (primary), redwood-7B-multilingual (fast/baseline), redwood-13B-64k (fallback for low-confidence responses).
3) Metrics: BLEU/chrF for NMT-style tasks, task-specific accuracy for intent classification, and a 3-point human quality label for naturalness/brand-voice.
4) Failure handling: tie low-confidence results to fallback model or rule-based path; we'll prototype that in the POC.

Attachments: prompt_sets_multilingual_v1.zip (prompt templates + locales), benchmark_run_instructions.md (how our harness runs), sample_eval_results_20270405.csv (format example).

Next steps:
- I'll upload the Drive folder with the eval harness (link below) and provision a shared evaluation dashboard.
- Can we schedule a 30-min alignment next Wed (Apr 14) to confirm exact locales and success thresholds?
- If procurement wants an initial SOW/contract sketch, I'll loop in PMM and legal.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3EvalDriveLink (eval folder)
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-2027-GLX-031

Happy to adjust depending on your priorities — thanks, Elena.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few quick clarifications before we lock the POC scope:

1) Locale nuance: French (FR) and Italian (IT) are higher priority for us due to brand voice and legal phrasing in product content. We need examples where legal/claims language is preserved verbatim. Can you provide a few sample outputs (EN->FR/IT) from the recommended models?

3) Latency: 500ms p50 is ambitious for 13B models on larger sequences — can you share previous latency profiles (p50/p95) for similar workloads?

Also CC'ing our procurement alias (procurement@globexretail.eu) to start contract questions.

Hi Elena —

Great questions. Quick answers below, plus links and sample artifacts.

1) Sample outputs: attached in the Drive folder is a small sample set (EN->FR/IT/DE/ES/JA) with outputs from both redwood-7B-multilingual and redwood-13B-multilingual-quant. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3EvalDriveLink
- Note: redwood-13B-multilingual-quant tends to preserve legal phrasing better in our internal tests; 7B is faster but sometimes more permissive with paraphrasing. We'll include an exact-preservation test in the eval prompts.

2) Data residency & audit logs: we can run the eval in your EU VPC/private deployment (data never leaves your region) and enable 12-month audit log retention. I'll attach the compliance checklist and a short SOC2-friendly runbook after we confirm NDA.

3) Latency profiles: for sequences ~150 tokens we typically see p50=300-450ms on our dedicated 13B-quant pool and p95 around 900ms; I added a benchmarking link in the eval folder with the raw numbers. If you need lower latency we can evaluate the 7B profile or experiment with batching/confidence-based routing.

POC ask: if procurement is open, can we get a quick LOI for a 30-day eval? That will let us provision dedicated capacity in your EU region. I've added the HubSpot deal ID (DEAL-2027-GLX-031) to keep things tracked.

Proposed meeting: Wed Apr 14, 09:30 CEST — does that work?

Thanks — attaching: benchmark_run_instructions.md and sample_eval_results_20270405.csv.

On Tue, Apr 6, 2027 at 09:05, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Elena —

Notes:
- Quantization/regression: when we run the 13B-quant model we include a regression gate that checks for token-level distribution shifts against baseline samples. If we see >5% drop in safety/precision signals for a locale, we auto-flag for human review.
- Confidence routing: we can instrument per-response confidence and route low-confidence FR/IT outputs to the redwood-13B-64k fallback (higher-context) or to a human-in-the-loop.
- Metrics to collect: BLEU, chrF, exact-preserve-rate (for legal phrasing), human-rated NPS-style score (1-3). We should include a small EU native-speaker panel for FR/IT to rate brand-voice.

I'll prepare a short runbook for the threshold checks and share the first sample eval CSV (sample_eval_results_20270405.csv) to show expected columns.

-rishi
